context_requirements: Expression of EP1/EP4 prostanoid receptors or COX-1/COX-2 enzymes
Active endogenous prostanoid synthesis or exogenous prostanoid tone
Intact Gs/cAMP or Gq/Ca2+ signaling downstream of the targeted receptor
Cell lines with low basal prostanoid signaling may show little response
falsifiers: No consistent change in PTGS2 or immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN) at 6 h across responsive lines
No reduction in proliferation or cell-cycle genes at 24 h in any line
Strong and uniform transcriptional response in all nine lines, including lines lacking prostanoid receptor expression
Changes indistinguishable from generic stress or cytotoxicity without any prostaglandin-pathway-specific signature

evidence.supports: Gs/cAMP signaling can modulate apoptosis and Bak expression via CREB and AP-1, indicating that G-protein-coupled prostanoid receptor signaling can influence transcriptional programs
cAMP signaling downstream of Gs-coupled receptors can regulate Bcl-xL and apoptosis, supporting a link between prostanoid receptor antagonism and cell survival pathways

changes: Removed PTGS2 from proximal_up because antagonism of prostanoid receptors does not directly induce PTGS2 transcription; PTGS2 is a target of the same pathway and would more likely be unchanged or down.

Removed PTGS2 from proximal_down because the mechanism does not directly repress PTGS2 transcription; PTGS2 is not a receptor and its downregulation is not a proximal consequence of receptor antagonism.
Removed PTGS2 from late_up because there is no direct mechanism for prostanoid receptor antagonism to induce PTGS2 at 24 h.
Removed MMP2 from proximal_down because MMP2 is not a known direct target of prostanoid receptor antagonism and its direction is not justified.
Removed TIMP2 from proximal_down because TIMP2 is not a known direct target of prostanoid receptor antagonism and its direction is not justified.

Removed generic proliferation and stress genes (CCNA2, CCNB1, CCNB2, CDK1, CDC20, BUB1B, AURKA, AURKB, PLK1, TOP2A, MCM3, PCNA, MYBL2, E2F2, MELK) from late_down because they are generic proliferation markers rather than proximal prostanoid receptor targets.

Removed generic stress genes (CDKN1A, GADD45A, GADD45B, TSC22D3, DUSP4, DUSP6, IER3, SOCS2, ZFP36, NFIL3, CEBPD, CEBPA, HMOX1, SQSTM1) from late_up because they are generic stress or proliferation genes rather than specific prostanoid receptor targets.
Removed generic proliferation and stress genes from proximal_up and proximal_down lists to maintain specificity for prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Adjusted line_response for A549 from moderate to weak because A549 has a KRAS mutation and may not show a strong prostanoid receptor antagonist response.
Adjusted line_response for HEPG2 from moderate to weak because HEPG2 has TP53 wild-type but may not have strong prostanoid signaling.
Adjusted line_response for HT29 from moderate to weak because HT29 has a BRAF mutation and may not show a strong prostanoid receptor antagonist response.
Adjusted line_response for HCC515 from moderate to weak because HCC515 has a TP53 mutation and may not show a strong prostanoid receptor antagonist response.
Adjusted line_response for MCF7 from weak to moderate because MCF7 expresses prostanoid receptors and may respond to prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Adjusted line_response for PC3 from weak to moderate because PC3 expresses prostanoid receptors and may respond to prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Adjusted line_response for VCAP from weak to moderate because VCAP expresses prostanoid receptors and may respond to prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Adjusted line_response for A375 from weak to moderate because A375 has a BRAF mutation and may show a moderate response to prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Adjusted line_response for HA1E from weak to moderate because HA1E is an immortalized normal cell line and may show a moderate response to prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Changed kinetics from slow to moderate because prostanoid receptor antagonism can affect immediate-early genes at 6 h and cell-cycle genes at 24 h.
Changed magnitude at 6h from weak to moderate because prostanoid receptor antagonism can induce immediate-early genes.
Changed magnitude at 24h from moderate to weak because the effect on proliferation genes may be modest.
Removed evidence PMID 19381065 because the abstract does not directly support the claim about prostanoid receptor antagonism.
Removed evidence PMID 18059134 because the abstract does not directly support the claim about prostanoid receptor antagonism.
